- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates downside risk; increase forecast lows by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); apply a 1–3 day decay filter to smooth out immediate post-spike peaks.
- For 10+ day horizons, model tends to overfit recent trends; apply a 3–5 day moving average to dampen momentum bias.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; introduce a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment drops below 0.2 after 7 days, reduce forecast by 3–7% for remaining days.
- Mean reversion is stronger in 15–30 day horizons; if forecast exceeds 2σ above recent 10-day mean, cap at 1.5–2σ above mean for next 5 days.
